Choose which side receives the redstone control signal. Any side reads all sides except the sensor output. North, south, east and west are compass directions.

Choose the travel direction whose filter you want to edit. North → South means travelling south. Shared default applies to directions without a custom filter. Selecting a direction here does not change its rules.

Always runs whenever there is enough energy. Redstone ON runs while any connected emitter receives a signal. Redstone OFF runs while none receive a signal. All three need FE unless the server has set the energy cost to zero.

screen.fieldemitters.guide.title: Field Emitters guide
screen.fieldemitters.guide.open_help: Open the guide for building fields and using the tuner.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.setup.title: First field
screen.fieldemitters.guide.setup.step1: Place two emitter posts in a straight line, either north to south or east to west. Make sure there is room above them.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.setup.step2: Connect an FE cable, generator or energy cell to an emitter. Connected emitters share their stored energy.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.setup.step3: Use Field to switch the network on or off. Settings apply as you change them.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.setup.step4: Turn on chooses whether the field needs a redstone signal. A signal at one emitter controls the network. It still needs FE.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.rails.title: Rails & bridges
screen.fieldemitters.guide.rails.step1: Place Field Rails on opposite sides of the gap, facing each other. Mount each rail against a solid block.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.rails.step2: Add pairs beside the first pair to make the bridge wider. Connect an energy source to any rail.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.rails.step3: Bridge mode turns the field horizontal and sets it to support everyone, including you. It also turns damage off.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.rails.step4: For a tall wall, stack rail pairs vertically and choose a vertical Field shape. Set Blocking for movement through the wall.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.towers.title: Domes & spheres
screen.fieldemitters.guide.towers.step1: Place a Projection Tower with seven clear blocks of height. Connect an energy source to its base.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.towers.step2: Choose Dome or Full sphere in Connections, then set Radius. This example shows a dome forming.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.towers.step3: A dome reaches up to four blocks below the tower to meet the ground. You can build and move around inside it.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.towers.step4: A full sphere extends below the tower as well. The inside stays open. Keep the chunks containing the field loaded.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.blocking.step: With Block selected, the field stops whatever matches your filter. With Allow selected only, it lets those matches through and blocks everything else.
Here, Hostile is selected and Passive is off, so the sheep can walk through. Age and the advanced filters let you narrow the selection.
Use Mob list, Item list or Player list for specific entries. A blacklist blocks the listed entries; a whitelist allows only those entries.
Use Sample type to select a mob type, or Sample individual for one particular mob. You can also drag supported JEI ingredients into lists.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.directions.st: The shared default applies to any travel direction that does not have its own filter.
Select a travel direction, then choose Custom filter to give it a different rule. Here, the player can pass in one direction.
Cardinal rules use north, south, east and west. You can use them to block passage from one side and allow it from the other.
For a closed perimeter, choose Relative to set rules for entering and leaving. Hold the tuner to see the direction guides.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.sensor.title: Detection
screen.fieldemitters.guide.sensor.step1: The Sensor tab has its own filter. Here, both mobs can pass through, but only the zombie triggers the lamp.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.sensor.step2: Choose Pulse on crossing to send a redstone pulse after an entity passes all the way through. Touching the field alone will not trigger it.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.sensor.step3: Another crossing extends the current pulse instead of adding a second pulse afterward. The counter still records both crossings.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.sensor.step4: Choose On while touching to keep the signal on while an entity touches the field. This also works when the field blocks it.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.damage.title: Contact damage
screen.fieldemitters.guide.damage.step1: Enable damage in the Damage tab, then set the amount and time between hits. Two health points equal one heart.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.damage.step2: Damage has its own filters and direction settings. Use them to choose which entities get hurt when they touch the field.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.damage.step3: A player with an access card can still take damage while passing through. Check the Damage filter if card holders should be safe.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.damage.step4: Fizzle particles in Damage turns the damage particles on or off. Damage sounds is in Sounds. Appearance controls their color.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.cards.title: Access cards
screen.fieldemitters.guide.cards.step1: A blocked player can use an access card if you enable card passage. Open Access, then Access cards to set it up.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.cards.step2: The field owner can issue a card for a group. Turn on card passage and add that group to the field's allowed groups.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.cards.step3: The player can now pass with their card. A player specifically named in the blocklist will still be stopped.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.cards.step4: Revoke cards disables the group's existing cards on every field that accepts them. Management permission is set separately.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.checkpoint.st: Open Access, then Inventory checkpoint. Choose the players, travel directions and contraband items to check.
The item list can match the entries you add, or everything except those entries. The checkpoint only checks players who match its filter.
You can have the checkpoint signal an alert, stop the player, drop the items on the entry side, or send them to adjacent storage.
If storage fills up, the player keeps the items and is stopped at the checkpoint. Enable overflow drops to drop those items instead.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.networks.step: Right-click the tuner in the air to open the Field Manager. It shows loaded fields in your current dimension.
Select a field to rename it or open its controls remotely. Emitters can still link together while the field is turned off.
Settings normally apply to the whole network. In Connections, you can select one connection and give it different rules.
New networks are private. Open Access, then Field management to let other players change the settings.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.appearance.st: Choose a color preset in Appearance, or enter a six-digit hex code. You can also give the effects a different color.
The Pattern button cycles through hex lattice, smooth glow, drifting pixels and plasma.
This is the drifting pixels pattern. You can use it with any of the formation animations.
This is Plasma. For sound effects, open Sounds and choose a Sound set. You can also turn off individual sound types.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.trouble.title: Troubleshooting
screen.fieldemitters.guide.trouble.step1: If the field will not turn on, check its status in Overview. Make sure it has FE power and the correct redstone settings.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.trouble.step2: If emitters will not connect, check their alignment, range and ownership. Posts connect to posts, and rails connect to rails. Both must be loaded.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.trouble.step3: If something gets through, check Blocking, the travel direction, Skip owner and access cards. The Sensor filter only controls detection.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.trouble.step4: Once the field switches off, you can walk through it even while it fades out. Any plants in its path will return.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.formations.st: Choose a formation animation in Appearance. This example uses Scan line with the hex pattern.
Hex assembly builds the field a cell at a time. Wait for it to finish forming before relying on the barrier.
Tracing ribs draws across the field as it forms. On towers, the animation follows the curved surface.
Projected seed grows from the middle. Formation also includes Sweep, Dissolve / reform, Fade, Laser curtain and Plasma dissolve.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.age.title: Adult & baby mobs
screen.fieldemitters.guide.age.step1: In Blocking, select Passive and set Age to Adults only. Adult sheep are stopped, while lambs can pass.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.age.step2: Set Age to Babies only to stop lambs and let adult sheep through.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.age.step3: Set Age to Any age to stop both. The age setting applies to the mobs selected by your filter.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.age.step4: You can also filter by age in Sensor. Here, both sheep can pass, but only the lamb triggers the signal.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.items.title: Items & type lists
screen.fieldemitters.guide.items.step1: Drops refers to items lying on the ground. Here, the field stops gunpowder while letting sheep through.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.items.step2: In Blocking, open Item list. Blacklist stops the listed items. Whitelist lets only those items through.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.items.step3: Drag supported items from JEI or the inventory panel into the list. In Mob list, you can use spawn eggs to select mobs.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.items.step4: Enter an ID such as minecraft:gunpowder for one item, or #namespace:tag for a tag. The Nonliving category includes projectiles and vehicles.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.equipment.ste: Right-click an emitter with the tuner to open its controls. Right-click the air to open the Field Manager.
Sneak-right-click a mob or player to sample them, or the air to sample yourself. Then use Sample type or Sample individual in a filter.
You can assign a key to Open Field Tuner in Minecraft's Controls menu. Keep the tuner in your inventory.
A card holder holds 16 cards. In your inventory, right-click the holder with a card on your cursor to insert it, or an empty cursor to remove one.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.automation.st: Datapacks can add field presets and filters, as well as change recipes and item or entity tags.
Server operators can use /fieldemitters export with an emitter's coordinates to export its settings as JSON for a preset.
A locked preset prevents changes through the tuner. After editing and reloading a preset, apply it again to update an existing field.
Where KubeJS is supported, server scripts can respond to crossings, contraband and power changes. The Automation wiki has examples.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.terrain.title: Terrain & plants
screen.fieldemitters.guide.terrain.step1: The field follows the ground between its posts. In this example, the path dips below the posts and has flowers growing in it.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.terrain.step2: The field extends down to the path. Plants in its way are stored while it is on.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.terrain.step3: The field also blocks passage through doors, gates and panes along its path.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.terrain.step4: Turn the field off or remove it to bring the plants back. They return as they were, without dropping items.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.s: Right-click an emitter to open its controls. Overview has the Enabled switch and redstone settings.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.r: Open Connections and click Bridge mode. This sets the shape and blocking rules together.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.t: In Connections, choose Dome or Full sphere with the Shape button. Use Radius to change the size.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.b: Open Blocking to choose what the field stops. Start with the categories, then use the lists or age setting if needed.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.d: In Blocking, open Travel directions. Choose which direction to edit, then select Custom filter to give it different rules.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.s: Open Sensor and use the Signal button to choose a crossing pulse or a signal that stays on during contact.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.d: Open Damage to choose what takes damage. Open Damage settings to set the amount and time between hits.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.c: Open Access, then Access cards to issue cards and choose which groups can pass through.
Open Access, then Inventory checkpoint to choose which items to check for and what to do with them.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.a: Open Appearance to change the field's color and pattern. Sound settings are in the Sounds tab.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.f: Use Formation in the Appearance tab to choose how the field forms when it turns on.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.a: In Blocking or Sensor, use Age to choose adults, babies or both.
screen.fieldemitters.guide.walkthrough.i: Open Item list in Blocking to choose which dropped items to stop. For items players are carrying, use Inventory checkpoint.
screen.fieldemitters.pages.checkpoint_ru: Choose a direction to view its rules. Select Custom filter before changing them. Viewing a direction does not change it.
screen.fieldemitters.pages.checkpoint_re: The redstone alert signals a match. Deny passage stops players carrying listed contraband. These options work independently.
screen.fieldemitters.pages.checkpoint_co: Keep items, drop them on the entry side, or send them to storage next to the emitter.
screen.fieldemitters.pages.checkpoint_st: Choose the side with the storage block. If it fills up, either stop the player or drop the remaining contraband on the entry side.
screen.fieldemitters.pages.card_filter_h: These groups use this player filter’s list mode. They do not grant passage by themselves. Issue and revoke cards under Access → Access cards.
screen.fieldemitters.pages.entity_detail: UUID and label restrictions apply to every target category in this filter. Leave them blank to match any entity.
